acceptance.given: Repair or runtime evidence handling is executed against the frozen historical record set.

oracle.expected: A before/after byte-and-membership manifest comparison reports identical record membership, paths, and bytes; only append-only evidence outside frozen records is permitted.
forbidden: Any frozen historical record is added, removed, relocated, renamed, or byte-modified.
oracle.observable: The validator emits a deterministic historical-record manifest comparison artifact with equal membership, paths, and byte hashes.

acceptance.then: The comparison passes and the frozen set remains unchanged.
acceptance.when: Before and after repair/runtime evidence generation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Mutate, remove, rename, relocate, or alter bytes of a frozen historical record and verify the historical-record manifest guard fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Add or preserve an append-only historical-record integrity check that snapshots frozen membership, repository-relative paths, and byte hashes before handling evidence, then compares them afterward.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert only the integrity-check implementation; preserve all frozen historical records and append-only evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: baseline manifest captured -> evidence operation runs -> manifest rechecked -> pass only on exact equality.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Historical membership, paths, and bytes compare exactly equal before and after the operation.

acceptance.given: The Toolchain exposes its supported Acceptance package route set.

oracle.expected: All declared supported Acceptance package routes resolve successfully and remain accessible through the route validator.
forbidden: A supported Acceptance package route is unavailable, removed, or resolves to an unsupported target.
oracle.observable: The route-validation result lists every supported Acceptance route with successful availability and target resolution.

acceptance.then: Supported Acceptance package routes remain available.
acceptance.when: When the supported route set is exposed or changed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Remove or point a declared supported Acceptance package route at an unavailable target and verify route validation fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Preserve and validate the supported Acceptance package route registry, resolving each route to an accessible repository-relative package target before accepting the route set.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore the prior supported-route registry and validator behavior without changing package identity or evidence schemas.

slice_hint.state_transition: route registry loaded -> each Acceptance route resolved -> availability and target checks pass -> route set exposed.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every supported Acceptance route is present, accessible, and resolves to its declared package target.

acceptance.given: A Replay Result has succeeded and declares dependency inputs for its execution.

oracle.expected: The successful Replay Result contains an independent dependency-verification record whose checks are performed separately from replay success and cover every declared dependency.
forbidden: A successful Replay Result is accepted without independent verification of its dependencies.
oracle.observable: The result artifact includes a dependency verification section with independently produced checks and a pass for each declared dependency.

acceptance.then: Dependencies are independently verified and recorded.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Return success while omitting or falsifying the independent dependency-verification record and verify acceptance fails.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require successful replay evaluation to invoke an independent dependency verifier and bind its per-dependency results into the Replay Result before success is emitted.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Revert verifier integration while retaining existing Replay Result schema compatibility; no successful result may bypass dependency checks.

slice_hint.state_transition: replay executes -> independent dependency verification executes -> dependency evidence bound -> success result emitted.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Success is emitted only when an independently generated verification record covers and passes every declared dependency.

acceptance.given: An aggregate execution runs under the NFR-7 bounded execution policy.

oracle.expected: The aggregate records one deterministic terminal state within the configured time/output budget; budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.
forbidden: The aggregate ends indeterminately, produces conflicting terminal states, or exceeds its budget without an unsuccessful terminal result.
oracle.observable: The execution result contains a single terminal-state record with deterministic classification, completion reason, and budget outcome.

acceptance.then: The aggregate reaches and records a deterministic terminal state.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Force aggregate timeout or conflicting terminal transitions and verify the execution is rejected unless one deterministic unsuccessful terminal state is recorded.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce bounded aggregate execution with a single terminal-state transition, deterministic classification, and explicit unsuccessful outcome on budget exhaustion.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore prior bounded-execution implementation while preserving terminal-state and budget fields for existing consumers.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate starts -> bounded work executes -> exactly one terminal transition (success, failure, or budget-exhausted failure).
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Exactly one deterministic terminal state is persisted; no run remains indeterminate and budget exhaustion is unsuccessful.
